words.note: Neutral, polite "I". With friends young people say "mình" (with "bạn") or, very common in Hanoi, "tớ" (with "cậu").
Links two nouns. Not used before adjectives: "Tôi khỏe" (I am well), not "Tôi là khỏe".

words.example_vi: Bạn ấy là bạn của tôi.
words.note: Used for people about your own age. For older or younger people use anh, chị, em, ông, bà, …
Comes at the end of the question.
người + country = nationality (người Việt Nam, người Mỹ, người Đức).

words.example_en: I want to go to Vietnam.

words.note: tiếng + country = language (tiếng Anh, tiếng Đức, tiếng Pháp).

words.example_vi: Bạn có nói tiếng Anh không?
Tôi học tiếng Việt mỗi ngày.
Em trai tôi là sinh viên.
words.example_en: My younger brother is a student.
words.note: A school pupil is "học sinh".

words.english: to do, to work, to make
words.example_en: What do you do (for a living)?
words.note: nghề = profession, job.
Answer: "Tôi ba mươi tuổi" (I am 30). For small children ask "Cháu mấy tuổi?".
In "có … không?" questions, "có" also means "yes".
At the end of a sentence it turns it into a yes/no question: "Bạn có khỏe không?"
"chúng ta" = we, including the person you are talking to.
Pronoun + ấy = he/she: anh ấy (he), chị ấy (she), bạn ấy (he/she, same age).
Casual "I" between friends of about the same age, paired with "bạn". Use "tôi" in neutral or formal situations.

words.example_vi: Tớ tên là Minh, còn cậu?
words.note: Very common among young people and students in the North, paired with "cậu". Only with friends.

words.example_en: Which school do you go to?
words.note: Friendly "you" between friends of the same age, paired with "tớ".

words.example_vi: Bọn mình là bạn cùng lớp.
words.note: Casual "we" among friends. Also "bọn tớ". "Chúng tôi" sounds formal.

words.example_vi: Lan là bạn thân của mình.

words.note: Young people ask this when they meet to find out who is older, so they know whether to say anh, chị or em.

words.example_vi: Sở thích của mình là chơi game và nghe nhạc.
words.example_en: My hobbies are gaming and listening to music.

words.english: to add as a friend (online); to make friends
words.example_en: Let's add each other on Zalo!
words.note: Zalo is the most popular chat app in Vietnam; young people also use Facebook Messenger and Instagram.

words.example_vi: Tối nay tớ nhắn tin cho cậu nhé.

words.note: Formal. In daily life people say "chào" + pronoun. To older people add "ạ": "Cháu chào bà ạ."
Usually followed by a pronoun: chào anh, chào chị, chào em, chào bạn.
Standard goodbye, a bit formal. Among friends young people often say "bye" (pronounced "bai"), "bye nhé" or "chào" + pronoun; to older people: "Em chào chị ạ."

words.example_vi: Chào chị, chị có khỏe không?
words.example_en: Hello, how are you? (to an older woman)
words.note: Standard, polite question. Among friends people also just ask "Khỏe không?" or "Dạo này thế nào?". To older people add "ạ": "Ông có khỏe không ạ?"
To be polite to older people add "ạ": "Cảm ơn anh ạ."

words.example_vi: – Cảm ơn bạn! – Không có gì.
words.note: Literally: "it's nothing".
Also "excuse me" to get attention. More polite with "ạ": "Xin lỗi chị ạ."
Polite "yes". In Hanoi people often say "dạ" or "dạ vâng" to elders, and add "ạ": "Vâng ạ."

words.example_vi: Chào chị, rất vui được gặp chị.
words.example_en: Hello, nice to meet you. (to an older woman)
words.note: Polite and standard. Among young people a simple "Chào bạn, mình là Lan." is also common.

words.example_en: What is your name? (to an older man)
words.note: For a man a bit older than you, or a man of similar age in polite situations.

words.example_en: How are you? (to an older woman)
words.note: For a woman a bit older than you, or a woman of similar age in polite situations.

words.example_en: What is your name? (to a younger person)
words.note: Also used by the younger person to say "I" when talking to an older person.
For a man of your grandparents' age; also "Mr." Speak politely: add "ạ" at the end ("Ông có khỏe không ạ?") and call yourself "cháu".

words.example_vi: Bà tôi sống ở Hà Nội.
words.note: For a woman of your grandparents' age; also "Mrs." Speak politely: add "ạ" at the end ("Cháu chào bà ạ.") and call yourself "cháu".

words.example_en: Hello, grandma. (polite, from a young person)
words.note: Put at the end of a sentence to show respect to older people. Very common in Hanoi.
Comes before the verb.

words.english: you (woman of your parents' age); aunt; female teacher
words.example_en: Hello. (politely, to a woman of your parents' age)
words.note: For a woman around your parents' age, and how students address a female teacher. Call yourself "cháu" (or "em" to a teacher) and add "ạ".

words.english: you (man of your parents' age); uncle
words.example_en: How are you? (politely, to a man of your parents' age)
words.note: For a man around your parents' age (younger than your father). Call yourself "cháu" and add "ạ".
Respectful "yes" to older people or customers. Often combined: "dạ vâng".

words.example_vi: Lâu rồi không gặp! Dạo này thế nào?
words.example_en: Long time no see! How have you been?
words.note: The natural way friends ask "how are you?". "Thế nào" is Northern (Southern: "sao").

words.example_vi: – Đi cà phê không? – Ừ, đi!
words.note: Only to friends or younger people. To older people say "dạ" or "vâng".
Young people often answer "ổn" or "cũng ổn" (I'm alright) instead of "khỏe".
Young people use English "bye" (said "bai") more often than "tạm biệt" with friends.

words.example_vi: Ơ, Lan! Lâu rồi không gặp!
words.example_en: Oh, Lan! Long time no see!

words.example_vi: Gia đình tôi có bốn người.
words.example_en: There are four people in my family.

words.example_vi: Mẹ tôi sống ở Hà Nội.
Anh trai tôi ba mươi tuổi.
words.example_en: My older brother is thirty years old.

words.example_vi: Chị gái tôi là bác sĩ.
words.example_en: My older sister is a doctor.
My younger sister is ten years old.

words.example_vi: Bạn có anh chị em không?

words.note: Also a classifier for animals (con mèo = cat) and how children say "I" to their parents.

words.example_vi: Con trai tôi học tiếng Anh.
Chồng tôi là người Việt Nam.

words.example_en: My wife likes to drink tea.

words.example_vi: Ông bà tôi sống ở Hà Nội.

words.note: Often dropped for family: "mẹ tôi" = "mẹ của tôi" (my mother).
Young people call themselves "cháu" when talking to ông, bà, cô, chú: "Cháu chào ông ạ."

words.example_vi: Người yêu mình là người Hà Nội.
words.note: Literally "loved person". Also "bạn trai" (boyfriend) and "bạn gái" (girlfriend). Often written "ny" in texts.
"bố" is Northern; in the South people say "ba".

words.example_vi: Tôi thích cà phê Việt Nam.
Cho tôi một cốc nâu đá.
words.example_en: An iced milk coffee for me, please.
words.note: Hanoi term ("brown + ice"). Hot version: "nâu nóng".

words.example_vi: Anh ấy uống cà phê đen không đường.
words.example_en: He drinks black coffee without sugar.
words.note: In Hanoi also just "đen đá" (iced black coffee).

words.example_vi: Em ơi, cho anh hai cốc trà đá.
words.example_en: Excuse me, two iced teas please.
words.note: In the North tea is also called "chè" (careful: "chè" is also a sweet dessert soup). "Trà đá" = cheap street iced tea in Hanoi.

words.example_en: A glass of water for me, please.
words.note: Also means "country": "Bạn là người nước nào?" (Which country are you from?)

words.example_vi: Tôi muốn một cốc nước cam.
words.example_en: I want a glass of orange juice.

words.example_vi: Cà phê này có đá không?
words.note: Also means "stone" and "to kick".
Same word for "road/street". ít = a little.

words.example_en: Two bottles of beer for me, please.
words.note: "Bia hơi" = fresh draft beer, a Hanoi specialty. chai = bottle.

words.example_vi: Tôi muốn một cốc sinh tố bơ.

words.note: quá after an adjective = too / so.

words.example_en: What do you want to drink?
Give me a cup of tea, please.
words.note: "Cho + pronoun …" is the standard way to order. Young people say "cho mình …", or to young staff "em ơi, cho anh / chị …".

words.example_vi: Một cốc cà phê, cảm ơn.
words.example_en: A cup of coffee, thank you.

words.example_vi: Cho tôi một cốc nước cam.
words.example_en: An orange juice for me, please.

words.example_vi: Cho chúng tôi hai cốc bia.
words.example_en: Two glasses of beer for us, please.
The orange juice is very good.
words.note: Comes before the adjective.

words.example_en: Want to go get bubble tea?
words.note: Hugely popular with young people. "Trân châu" = tapioca pearls.

words.example_vi: Tối nay đi trà chanh nhé!
words.example_en: Let's go for lime tea tonight!
words.note: Cheap Hanoi street drink. "Đi trà chanh" means hanging out and chatting on little plastic stools.

words.example_vi: Cà phê trứng là đặc sản Hà Nội.
words.example_en: Egg coffee is a Hanoi specialty.
words.note: Coffee topped with whipped egg yolk and sugar, invented in Hanoi.

words.example_vi: Cho mình một cốc cà phê muối.
words.note: Coffee with a salty cream topping; very trendy with young people.

words.example_vi: Cho mình một trà sữa, ít đá, ít đường nhé.
words.example_en: A milk tea, less ice and less sugar, please.
words.note: Also "không đá" (no ice) and "ít ngọt" (less sweet).
Literally "100 percent": finish your glass. People also shout "Một, hai, ba, dô!" when they toast.

words.example_vi: Em ơi, cho anh xem thực đơn.
words.example_en: Excuse me, can I see the menu?
words.note: Many places also just say "menu".

words.example_vi: Em ơi, cho chị một cốc nước.
words.example_en: Excuse me, a glass of water please.
words.note: Used for younger staff. If the person is older: "anh ơi" / "chị ơi".

words.example_vi: Cho tôi một bát phở bò.
words.example_en: A bowl of beef pho, please.
words.note: phở bò = beef pho, phở gà = chicken pho. Pho originated in the North.

words.example_vi: Cho tôi thêm một bát cơm.
words.example_en: One more bowl of rice, please.

words.example_vi: Bún chả Hà Nội rất ngon.
words.example_en: Hanoi bun cha is very delicious.
words.note: A famous Hanoi dish.

words.example_vi: Tôi ăn cơm với gia đình.
words.example_en: I eat (a meal) with my family.
What do you want to eat?

words.note: Also "thanh toán" (to pay).
tiền = money.

words.example_vi: Trà đá ba nghìn đồng một cốc.
words.example_en: Iced tea is three thousand dong a glass.

words.note: "Không cay" = not spicy.
chờ / đợi = to wait.
Softens a request or suggestion.

words.english: at, in; to be (located), to stay

words.example_vi: Hà Nội là một thành phố đẹp.

words.example_en: My house is near the market.

words.example_vi: Nhà hàng này có phở ngon.
Chúng ta đi quán cà phê nhé!
words.note: quán = small shop / eatery (quán phở, quán bia).

words.example_vi: Em gái tôi học ở trường này.
words.example_en: My younger sister studies at this school.
words.note: trường đại học = university.

words.example_vi: Bố tôi làm ở bệnh viện.
words.example_en: My father works at a hospital.
My mother goes to the market.

words.example_vi: Xin lỗi, nhà vệ sinh ở đâu?
words.example_en: Excuse me, where is the toilet?
Hoan Kiem Lake is very beautiful.

words.note: "lớn" also means big and is a bit more formal.

words.example_vi: Quán cà phê này nhỏ nhưng đẹp.
words.example_en: This café is small but pretty.
words.note: In the North "bé" is also very common. nhưng = but.

words.example_en: The hotel is near the lake.

words.example_vi: Hồ Hoàn Kiếm ở Hà Nội.
words.example_en: Hoan Kiem Lake is in Hanoi.
words.note: Hanoi has many lakes: Hồ Hoàn Kiếm, Hồ Tây (West Lake).
"đấy" at the end makes the question sound casual and friendly.

words.example_vi: Cuối tuần đi phố đi bộ không?
words.example_en: Want to go to the walking street this weekend?
words.note: Around Hoàn Kiếm Lake the streets are car-free on weekend evenings, a favourite hangout.

words.example_vi: Trung tâm thương mại này to quá!
words.note: Young people often just say the mall's name, e.g. "đi Vincom".
English loanword that young Vietnamese use all the time: "đi cà phê chill".
Slang. "Xịn xò" is an even more playful version.
Slang, literally "peak". Also "đỉnh của chóp" (the absolute best).

words.example_vi: Em gái mình là học sinh lớp mười.
words.example_en: My younger sister is in 10th grade.
words.note: For university students say "sinh viên".

words.example_vi: Lớp mình có ba mươi bạn.
words.example_en: There are thirty people in our class.
words.note: "lớp mười" = 10th grade.

words.example_vi: Minh là bạn cùng lớp của tớ.
Thầy ơi, em hỏi một câu được không ạ?
words.example_en: Sir, can I ask a question?
words.note: Students call a male teacher "thầy" and a female teacher "cô", call themselves "em" and add "ạ".

words.example_en: Which subject do you like best?
words.note: môn Toán = maths, môn Văn = literature, môn tiếng Anh = English.

words.example_en: Have you done the homework yet?
words.note: "bài tập về nhà" = homework. "chưa?" at the end = "yet?".

words.example_vi: Mai có bài kiểm tra tiếng Anh.
words.note: "Mai" (short for "ngày mai") = tomorrow.
Vietnam grades from 0 to 10; "điểm mười" is top marks.

words.example_en: I'm so scared of failing the exam!
words.note: "trượt" is Northern (Southern: "rớt"). Passing is "thi đỗ" or "qua môn".
"Em không hiểu ạ" = I don't understand (polite, to a teacher).

words.example_vi: Em có một câu hỏi ạ.
Cô nhắc lại được không ạ?
words.note: Very handy for learners. Also "nói chậm thôi" = speak more slowly.
"Cho tớ mượn …" = lend me … / can I borrow …

words.example_vi: Tớ quên vở ở nhà rồi.
words.example_en: I left my notebook at home.
words.note: "vở" is Northern (Southern: "tập").
"muộn" is Northern (Southern: "trễ").

words.english: to be absent; to have no class
words.example_vi: Hôm nay tớ nghỉ học vì bị ốm.
words.example_en: I'm off school today because I'm sick.
words.note: "ốm" = sick (Northern). Skipping class on purpose is "trốn học", or "bùng học" in Hanoi slang.

words.example_vi: Tan học đi trà sữa không?
Tối nay bọn mình học nhóm nhé.
words.example_en: Let's have a study group tonight.

words.english: to rush to meet a deadline
words.example_vi: Đêm nay tớ phải chạy deadline.
words.example_en: I have to rush a deadline tonight.
words.note: Student slang mixing English and Vietnamese; "deadline" is used as is.

words.example_vi: Mình ở ký túc xá của trường.
words.example_en: I live in the university dorm.
words.note: Students usually just say "KTX" (ca-tê-ích).

words.example_vi: Ra căng tin ăn gì đi!
words.example_en: Let's go grab something at the canteen!

words.english: to travel, to go on a trip
words.example_vi: Hè này bọn mình đi du lịch Sa Pa.
words.example_en: This summer we're going on a trip to Sa Pa.

words.example_vi: Cuối tuần đi phượt Hà Giang không?
words.example_en: Road trip to Hà Giang this weekend?
words.note: Youth slang for adventurous, budget travel, often by motorbike. A backpacker is "dân phượt".

words.example_vi: Cho mình hai vé đi Hạ Long.
words.example_en: Two tickets to Hạ Long, please.
words.note: vé tàu = train ticket, vé máy bay = plane ticket, vé xe = bus ticket.

words.example_vi: Từ đây ra sân bay mất bao lâu?
words.example_en: How long does it take from here to the airport?
words.note: Hanoi's airport is Nội Bài.

words.example_vi: Máy bay cất cánh lúc mấy giờ?
words.example_en: What time does the plane take off?

words.example_vi: Bọn mình đi tàu đêm vào Huế.
words.example_en: We're taking the night train to Huế.
words.note: Also "tàu hỏa". "ga" = (train) station: ga Hà Nội.

words.example_vi: Xe buýt số mấy đi Hồ Tây?
words.example_en: Which bus number goes to West Lake?

words.example_vi: Mình đặt xe giường nằm đi Sa Pa rồi.
words.example_en: I've booked a sleeper bus to Sa Pa.
words.note: Overnight long-distance bus with beds, popular with young travellers.

words.example_vi: Muộn rồi, gọi Grab về nhé.
words.example_en: It's late, let's get a Grab home.
words.note: Grab is the ride-hailing app everyone uses. "Grab bike" = motorbike, "Grab car" = car. Also "xe ôm" = motorbike taxi.

words.example_vi: Thuê xe máy một ngày bao nhiêu tiền?
words.example_en: How much is it to rent a motorbike for a day?

words.example_vi: Đến ngã tư thì rẽ trái.
words.note: "rẽ" is Northern (Southern: "quẹo").

words.example_vi: Anh ơi, rẽ phải ở đây ạ.
Anh ơi, cho em xuống đây ạ.
words.note: For a driver older than you. Change the pronoun as needed: "cho mình xuống đây nhé".

words.example_vi: Bọn mình bị lạc đường rồi!
Đi bộ ra hồ mất bao lâu?
words.example_en: How long does it take to walk to the lake?
What time does the train leave?
words.note: "Bây giờ là mấy giờ?" = What time is it now?

words.example_vi: Cho mình xem hộ chiếu được không?

words.note: Young travellers mostly stay in a "homestay" (the English word is used).

words.example_vi: Mật khẩu wifi là gì ạ?
words.note: "wifi" is said "wai-phai". Also "pass wifi".

words.example_en: Could you take a photo of us?
words.note: "ảnh" is Northern (Southern: "hình").

words.example_vi: Quán này nhiều góc sống ảo lắm!
words.example_en: This café has lots of Instagram spots!
words.note: Youth slang, literally "virtual living". Taking photos at a famous spot is also called "check-in".

words.example_vi: Mùa hè bọn mình hay đi biển.
words.example_en: In summer we often go to the beach.

words.example_vi: Sa Pa có nhiều núi đẹp.
words.example_en: Sa Pa has many beautiful mountains.

words.example_vi: Chị ơi, hết bao nhiêu ạ?
words.note: The natural question when paying for several things.

words.example_vi: Đắt quá! Bớt cho em đi.
words.example_en: That's too expensive! Give me a discount.
words.note: "đắt" is Northern (Southern: "mắc").

words.example_en: This place is cheap and good.
words.note: "Rẻ mà ngon" (cheap but tasty) is the highest praise for a street-food place.

words.example_vi: Ở chợ phải mặc cả nhé.
words.example_en: At the market you have to bargain.
words.note: Northern word; you'll also hear "trả giá".

words.english: to reduce (the price), to give a discount
words.example_vi: Bớt cho em một chút được không ạ?
words.example_en: Could you knock a bit off the price?

words.example_vi: Hôm nay giảm giá năm mươi phần trăm.
words.note: Young people also just say "sale".

words.example_vi: Mua hai tặng một, đang khuyến mại đấy!
words.example_en: Buy two get one free, there's a promotion on!
words.note: "khuyến mại" is Northern (Southern: "khuyến mãi"). tặng = to give as a gift.

words.example_vi: Cốc trà sữa này năm mươi k.
words.note: Young people say "k" (pronounced "ca") for nghìn: "ba mươi k" = 30,000.

words.example_vi: Cái áo này hai lít thôi.
words.note: Slang, literally "litre". "Củ" = one million: "năm củ" = 5,000,000.

words.example_vi: Ở đây chỉ nhận tiền mặt.
Em chuyển khoản được không ạ?
words.example_en: Can I pay by bank transfer?
words.note: Most people in Vietnam pay by scanning a QR code with their banking app ("quét mã QR").

words.example_vi: Chị ơi, chị chưa trả tiền thừa cho em.
words.example_en: Excuse me, you haven't given me my change.
words.note: "tiền thừa" is Northern (Southern: "tiền thối").

words.english: to treat (pay for someone); to invite
words.note: Among friends people often take turns paying ("mời") instead of splitting.
Also "chia đều" (split evenly) or slang "cưa đôi" (go halves).

words.example_vi: Mua được giá này là hời lắm!
words.example_en: Getting it at this price is a great deal!

words.example_vi: Quán này chặt chém khách du lịch.
words.note: Slang, literally "chop and slash".

words.example_vi: Cậu mua cái này ở đâu thế?
words.note: "thế" at the end of a question sounds casual (Northern).

words.example_vi: Chị bán cái này bao nhiêu ạ?
words.example_en: How much are you selling this for?

words.note: Young people also say "free": "freeship" = free delivery.
